{{< include ../_disclaimer.qmd >}}

# Question

In spring 2026 Hearts & Flowers got a redesign ("version 2"). Two changes were
intended: a feedback sound ("ding") and a third mixed block run at different
speeds. Did the revision help? Specifically: does the ding help or hurt, does
the new form buy reliability, and does it remove the known ceiling? The two
changes shipped together, so they are confounded by design; the strategy here
is to find outcomes that only one of them should move.

Data: `levante_data_latest:e9pf:v3_17` (scores, processed trials) plus the
**raw** per-site `trials`/`runs`/`variants` tables (13 sites, pulled
2026-10-15 by [`_prep_hf_v2.R`](_prep_hf_v2.R); derivations in
[`_hf_v2_common.R`](_hf_v2_common.R)).

```{r setup}
source(here::here("common.R"))
source(here::here("tasks/_hf_v2_common.R"))

scores <- readRDS(here("data/scores_latest_v3_17.rds")) |>
  filter(task_id == "hearts-and-flowers", !is.na(score)) |>
  distinct(run_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(run_id, theta = score, theta_se = score_se)

age_band <- \(a) cut(a, c(0, 6, 8, 10, 20), right = FALSE,
                     labels = c("<6", "6-8", "8-10", "10+"))
age_band5 <- \(a) cut(a, c(0, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20), right = FALSE,
                      labels = c("<6", "6-8", "8-10", "10-12", "12+"))

runs <- hf_run_struct |>
  left_join(hf_runs |> select(run_id, dataset, user_id, age, time_started,
                              stop_reason, variant_name, variant_created),
            by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(scores, by = "run_id")
complete_runs <- runs |> filter(grepl("complete \\(", layout))
scored_runs <- runs |> filter(!grepl("heavy", layout), !is.na(theta))
```

# 1. What changed, and which variants carry it

The redesign is core-tasks PR #442 (merged 2026-04-21, first shipped in task
version 1.1.2), gated on the **variant parameter `taskVersion === 2`**. That
parameter isn't exported to the Redivis `variants` table, but every variant
created from 2026-04-23 on runs the new form, and every variant created
2025-07-21 (the legacy `de` / `es-CO` / `English (North America) - Legacy`
variants) runs the old form, **regardless of code version**: old variants still
produce the 32-trial mixed block on code 1.3.17.

```{r variant-table}
runs |>
  filter(layout != "incomplete") |>
  count(form, variant_name, variant_created = substr(variant_created, 1, 10), layout) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = layout, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(form, variant_created) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "H&F variants by intended form (complete runs only; variant names repeat across site datasets)")
```

What v2 changes, read from the code:

| | v1 (old) | v2 (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Response deadline | **none** (configured presentation times were dead code) | pure blocks 3000 ms; mixed 3000 / 2000 / 1500 ms |
| Mixed block | 32 trials, untimed | 48 trials = 3 segments × 16, "going faster" instructions between |
| Feedback | none on test trials | **coin sound if correct, fail sound if not, every test trial** |
| No response | impossible | `response = null`, scored incorrect |
| Early stop | effectively none (`maxIncorrect` = 100) | **shared rule: stop if > 6 of the last 10 test trials are wrong** |
| `heavyInstructions` variants | — | mixed block cut to the first 16 trials |

Note that the early-stop rule's code comment says "4 of the last 10" but the
code tests `> 6`. Timeouts count as errors for it.

Scoring is unchanged across forms: the released `multigroup_dataset` Rasch
model uses the same item uids (`hf_{block}_{stim}_{start|stay|switch}`) for
both, and `recode_hf()` still marks every response faster than 200 ms or
slower than 2000 ms incorrect. (I checked whether processing drops timeouts.
It does not: all raw no-response trials are in the processed table, scored
incorrect.)

# 2. Mechanics: the new segments make the task harder only through time

```{r mechanics}
mech <- hf_test |>
  semi_join(complete_runs, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(block)) |>
  group_by(form, block, segment, window) |>
  summarise(trials = n(),
            correct_side_if_answered = mean(correct[!timeout] %in% TRUE),
            timeout = mean(timeout),
            rt_over_2s = mean(rt_numeric > 2000, na.rm = TRUE),
            scored_correct = mean(sc_pipeline),
            median_rt = median(rt_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(block = factor(block, c("hearts", "flowers", "mixed"))) |>
  arrange(form, block, segment)

knitr::kable(mech, digits = 3,
             caption = "Trial-level mechanics, complete runs. window = response deadline (Inf = untimed v1). scored_correct = as released (timeouts and RT outside 200-2000 ms are errors).")
```

Within v2 the three mixed segments differ only in their deadline (the
feedback is constant), so they isolate the timing manipulation. Shortening the
window from 3 s to 2 s to 1.5 s raises timeouts from 0.6% to 2.9% to 8.3%,
and that is most of the drop in scored accuracy (.89 → .83); the rest is a
small decline in accuracy on answered trials. The faster segments add
difficulty mainly by making children miss the window.

Across forms, the bigger effect is on slow responses. Untimed v1 children
answered after 2 s on 6–15% of trials, all of which `recode_hf()` scores
incorrect. Under v2's deadlines and feedback that share falls to 0–2.5%. One
mismatch follows: in the 3-s windows (pure blocks and mixed segment 1), a
correct 2–3 s response plays the coin but is scored wrong (0.3–2.5% of those
trials).

```{r rt-distributions, fig.height = 3.8, fig.width = 11}
rt_panels <- hf_test |>
  semi_join(complete_runs, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(block), !timeout, rt_numeric > 0, rt_numeric < 4000) |>
  mutate(panel = case_when(block != "mixed" ~ "pure blocks",
                           form == "v1" ~ "v1 mixed",
                           TRUE ~ paste0("v2 mixed, ", window / 1000, " s")),
         panel = factor(panel, c("pure blocks", "v1 mixed", "v2 mixed, 3 s",
                                 "v2 mixed, 2 s", "v2 mixed, 1.5 s")))
windows <- tibble(panel = factor(c("pure blocks", "v2 mixed, 3 s", "v2 mixed, 2 s",
                                   "v2 mixed, 1.5 s"), levels(rt_panels$panel)),
                  window = c(3000, 3000, 2000, 1500))
ggplot(rt_panels, aes(rt_numeric, fill = form)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .45, colour = NA, adjust = .8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2000, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(data = windows, aes(xintercept = window), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1000, 2000, 3000), labels = c("0", "1", "2", "3")) +
  labs(x = "Response time (s)", y = "Density", fill = "Form",
       title = "Response times by block: v1's slow tail vs v2's windows",
       subtitle = "Red: v2 response window. Dashed: the 2000 ms cutoff recode_hf() scores as an error. Answered trials of complete runs.")
```

The untimed v1 distributions have a long right tail past 2 s, all of which
is scored as error. v2's windows cut the tail off, and in the 2-s and 1.5-s
segments the whole distribution shifts left as children speed up.

# 3. Many more v2 runs end early

```{r completion}
runs |>
  filter(!grepl("heavy", layout)) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n_distinct(form) == 2) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(form) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), incomplete = mean(layout == "incomplete"), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Share of runs that end before the last trial, sites that ran both forms")

last_trial <- hf_test |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  slice_max(trial_index, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(run_id, last_block = block, last_segment = segment)

runs |>
  filter(layout == "incomplete") |>
  left_join(last_trial, by = "run_id") |>
  count(form, where_stopped = paste(last_block, coalesce(as.character(last_segment), ""))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Where incomplete runs stop (block and mixed segment)")

runs |>
  filter(form == "v2", layout == "incomplete") |>
  count(stop_reason) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "stop_reason for incomplete v2 runs (logged from 2026-07-31 only)")
```

About a quarter of v2 runs stop early (29% at sites that ran both forms),
against ~8% of v1 runs. Most v2 stops (371 of 581) fall in the 2-s and 1.5-s
segments, and 293 of the 343 stops with a logged reason are `errorOut`. That is the rule working as written: timeouts count as errors, so
a child who can't keep up with the 1.5-s pace is stopped. The truncation is
response-dependent, so θ estimates from the observed trials stay valid, but
these children lose their hardest trials and many leave the task on a run of
failures.

# 4. Floor and ceiling: the floor nearly disappears, the ceiling moves

```{r theta-by-age, fig.height = 4.8}
theta_age <- scored_runs |>
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 4, age < 14) |>
  group_by(form) |>
  mutate(at_cap = theta >= max(theta) - 0.05) |>
  ungroup()
ggplot(theta_age, aes(age, theta)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = at_cap), alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9) +
  geom_quantile(quantiles = c(.1, .5, .9), formula = y ~ splines::ns(x, 3),
                colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~form) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey55", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      labels = c("below the score cap", "at the score cap"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Released θ",
       title = "Released θ by age",
       subtitle = "All scored runs. Lines: 10th, 50th, 90th percentiles. The cap is the score of an error-free run.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r floor-ceiling-by-age, fig.height = 4.2}
run_acc <- hf_test |>
  semi_join(complete_runs, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(block)) |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(acc = mean(sc_pipeline),
            acc_mixed = mean(sc_pipeline[block == "mixed"]),
            perfect_mixed = all(sc_pipeline[block == "mixed"]), .groups = "drop")

ceiling_share <- scored_runs |>
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 4, age < 14) |>
  group_by(form) |>
  mutate(near_cap = theta >= max(theta) - 0.5) |>
  group_by(form, age_yr = floor(age)) |>
  summarise(n = n(), share = mean(near_cap), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(end = "Ceiling: θ within 0.5 logits of the cap (all scored runs)")
floor_share <- complete_runs |>
  inner_join(run_acc, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 4, age < 14) |>
  group_by(form, age_yr = floor(age)) |>
  summarise(n = n(), share = mean(acc_mixed <= .625), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(end = "Floor: mixed block ≤ 62.5% correct (complete runs)")

bind_rows(ceiling_share, floor_share) |>
  filter(n >= 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_yr, share, colour = form)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  facet_wrap(~end) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 13, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Share of runs", colour = "Form",
       title = "Floor and ceiling by age",
       subtitle = "Age bins with at least 15 runs; point size = runs. 62.5% correct is just above the 50% guessing rate.")
```

```{r ceiling-table}
complete_runs |>
  inner_join(run_acc, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(form, age = age_band(age)) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), mean_scored_acc = mean(acc),
            perfect_mixed = mean(perfect_mixed),
            acc_97_plus = mean(acc >= .97), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = -c(form, age)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Accuracy-based ceiling indicators by age band, complete runs. Note the mixed block is 32 trials in v1 and 48 in v2, so a perfect mixed block is harder to achieve in v2 regardless of difficulty.")

scored_runs |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(form) |>
  mutate(cap = max(theta)) |>
  group_by(form, age = age_band5(age)) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), at_cap = mean(theta >= cap - 0.05),
            within_half_logit = mean(theta >= cap - 0.5), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = -c(form, age)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "θ-scale ceiling by age band, all scored runs (cap = 4.0 in v1, 4.13 in v2)")
```

**The floor nearly disappears.** In v1, a third to a half of 5- and
6-year-olds scored near chance on the mixed block, and a fifth to a third of
7- to 9-year-olds. In v2 that share is under 5% at every age. Part of v1's floor
was slow responding: answers after 2 s are scored as errors (§2), and v1
children gave many of them.

**The ceiling can't be judged on released θ.** The released model scores v2
with item parameters calibrated on untimed v1 trials, so passing a 1.5-s
switch trial earns the same credit as an untimed pass, and the top of the v2
distribution is capped by items that are too easy for it. On released θ the
picture is mixed: fewer of the oldest children sit within half a logit of the
cap in v2 (10–12: 18% vs 4%; 12+: 25% vs 9%), but more 6- to 10-year-olds
sit exactly at it (4–6% vs about 1%). §11 refits both forms on one scale,
with the timed items calibrated separately, and that is the comparison to
use: **v2 does reduce the ceiling substantially.**

The accuracy indicators in the table are confounded too: the v2 mixed block
is half again as long (48 vs 32 trials), so a perfect block is harder to
achieve whatever the items' difficulty. (An earlier version of this section
read that as the fast segment cutting the ceiling.)

# 5. Reliability

## Split-half: v1's advantage is partly "slowness"

```{r split-half}
split_half <- function(trials, var) {
  halves <- trials |>
    arrange(run_id, trial_index) |>
    group_by(run_id) |>
    mutate(half = row_number() %% 2) |>
    group_by(run_id, half) |>
    summarise(x = mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = half, values_from = x)
  r <- cor(halves$`0`, halves$`1`, use = "complete.obs")
  2 * r / (1 + r)
}

sh_trials <- hf_test |>
  semi_join(complete_runs, by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(block)) |>
  mutate(slow = as.numeric(rt_numeric > 2000))

map_dfr(c("v1", "v2"), \(f) {
  d <- sh_trials |> filter(form == f)
  tibble(form = f, runs = n_distinct(d$run_id),
         scored_accuracy = split_half(d, "sc_pipeline"),
         side_correct_only = split_half(d, "sc_task"),
         share_slower_than_2s = split_half(d, "slow"))
}) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Odd/even split-half reliability (Spearman-Brown), complete runs")
```

On raw split-half, v1 looks more reliable (.96 vs .86). Part of that is a
stable individual difference v2 suppresses on purpose: in untimed v1, a
child's share of responses slower than 2 s is almost perfectly consistent
(.96), and those responses are scored as errors. Under v2's deadlines that
trait is much less reliable (.68). v1 still leads on side-correctness alone
(.93 vs .83).

## Model-based reliability of θ (all scored runs)

```{r empirical-rel}
scored_runs |>
  group_by(form, dataset) |>
  filter(n() >= 30) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), incomplete = mean(layout == "incomplete"),
            sd_theta = sd(theta), mean_se = mean(theta_se),
            reliability = var(theta) / (var(theta) + mean(theta_se^2)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Empirical reliability of released θ by dataset and form, all scored runs (incomplete runs included)")
```

Counting every scored run (including the children stopped early), v2's
model-based reliability is .85–.91 at most sites, about the same as v1's
.84–.93. Leipzig's wave 3 is the exception (.73): those children are older,
and their v2 scores are compressed (SD 1.1 vs 2.6 for v1). Restricting to
complete runs would understate v2 (it drops its weakest children), so these
all-runs numbers are the fair comparison. **The new form does not add
reliability; at best it holds it.**

## Test–retest

```{r retest}
pairs <- scored_runs |>
  filter(!is.na(user_id)) |>
  arrange(user_id, time_started) |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  mutate(theta2 = lead(theta), form2 = lead(form), dataset2 = lead(dataset),
         age2 = lead(age),
         gap_days = as.numeric(difftime(lead(time_started), time_started,
                                        units = "days"))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(theta2), gap_days >= 14, dataset == dataset2)

pairs |>
  group_by(dataset, forms = paste(form, form2, sep = " -> ")) |>
  filter(n() >= 10) |>
  summarise(pairs = n(), median_gap_days = median(gap_days),
            age_t2 = mean(age2, na.rm = TRUE), sd_theta_t2 = sd(theta2),
            r = cor(theta, theta2), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Retest correlation of θ by form pair (consecutive runs, >= 14 days apart, n >= 10)")
```

The only large cross-form sample is Leipzig: wave 1 → wave 2 (both v1)
retests at **.54**, while wave 2 (v1) → wave 3 (v2) retests at **.12**. Three
things are confounded in that drop: the form change, a much longer gap (~16
vs ~4 months), and range restriction in the older wave-3 sample (θ SD 1.1).
Western's small cross-form sample (n = 11, ~1 year) retests about like its
v1 → v1 pairs (.55 vs .58), while MPIB's 14 cross-form pairs (~7.5 months,
age ~7.5) come out negative (−.63). There is no adequate v2 → v2 retest yet
(Boston's 11 pairs are three weeks apart, in 4-year-olds).
**Cross-form continuity is not established, and the Leipzig number is a
warning for any longitudinal analysis that spans the switch.**

# 6. Age validity

```{r age-validity}
scored_runs |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n_distinct(form) == 2) |>
  group_by(dataset, form) |>
  filter(n() >= 30) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), mean_age = mean(age), sd_age = sd(age),
            r_theta_age = cor(theta, age),
            logits_per_year = coef(lm(theta ~ age))[2], .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "θ–age association within sites that ran both forms, all scored runs")
```

Age associations are weaker under v2 at most sites that ran both forms (the
exception is rural Colombia). Sample age ranges differ by wave and site, so
this is suggestive rather than decisive. It fits the compression seen above:
v2 lifts the low end, so younger children look more like older ones.

# 7. The ding: a clean feedback signature

Feedback should change what happens *after an error*. The pure blocks are the
best place to look, because the 3-s deadline almost never binds there (<1%
timeouts) and only the feedback differs.

```{r post-error}
post_error <- hf_test |>
  filter(!is.na(block), !timeout, !is.na(age)) |>
  arrange(run_id, trial_index) |>
  group_by(run_id, block) |>
  mutate(prev_error = lag(!(correct %in% TRUE))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(prev_error)) |>
  group_by(form, block, age = age_band(age), prev_error) |>
  summarise(trials = n(), acc = mean(correct %in% TRUE),
            rt = median(rt_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = prev_error, values_from = c(trials, acc, rt)) |>
  transmute(form, block = factor(block, c("hearts", "flowers", "mixed")), age,
            error_trials = trials_TRUE,
            acc_after_error = acc_TRUE, acc_after_correct = acc_FALSE,
            post_error_slowing_ms = rt_TRUE - rt_FALSE)

post_error |>
  arrange(block, age, form) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Post-error behaviour (side-correctness; timeouts excluded)")
```

```{r post-error-plot, fig.height = 4}
post_error |>
  filter(block != "mixed") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, y = acc_after_error, colour = form, group = form)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(aes(size = error_trials)) +
  facet_wrap(~block) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Age band", y = "Accuracy on the trial after an error",
       title = "With feedback, children recover from errors")
```

Without feedback (v1), children speed up after an error (negative
post-error slowing) and are often wrong again: post-error accuracy in the
flowers block is .41–.63, a signature of being stuck on the wrong rule. With
the coin/fail sound (v2), post-error slowing turns positive or near zero, and
post-error accuracy rises sharply in 7 of the 8 pure-block age cells
(flowers, ages 6–8: .47 → .73; 10+: .63 → .90; the exception is hearts at
8–10, from small counts).
Accuracy after a *correct* trial is the same in both forms, so this isn't a
difference in the samples' baseline ability.

**So the ding does what feedback should**: it breaks perseverative error runs.
Whether that "helps" depends on what the task should measure. v1's lower range
was partly children who never grasped or held the flower rule; v2 corrects
them within a few trials, which makes it more a measure of conflict
efficiency and less of rule acquisition. That shift accounts for much of the
low-end compression in sections 4–6.

# 8. Separating the two interventions

| Outcome | Moved by | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Post-error recovery, pure blocks | feedback | v1 → v2 at matched post-correct accuracy (§7) |
| Timeouts, early stops in mixed | timing | dose-response across v2's three segments, feedback constant (§2, §3) |
| Fewer slow (>2 s) responses | both | deadline caps them; feedback also speeds responses in the pure blocks, where the deadline barely binds |
| Fewer near-cap scores at 10+ | timing (likely) | the 1.5-s segment is the only part of v2 that is hard for older children (§2, §9) |
| Higher scored accuracy at young ages | both, mostly feedback + fewer slow errors | §4, §7 |
| Reliability, retest, age validity | not separable | only overall v1 vs v2 contrasts exist |

# 9. Timing, calibration, and the ceiling

The redesign's goal was to remove the ceiling and make the task harder for
older children while measuring the same constructs. This section asks how
well the timings serve that goal: where items of each timing sit relative to
children's abilities at each age, and whether shorter windows add
information about inhibition and switching or about something else.

## Where the released items sit

The released model is a Rasch model with a fixed guessing floor of 0.5,
calibrated on 1,671 runs (registry v2_3, August 2026), essentially all of
them untimed v1.

```{r released-items}
released <- readRDS(here("data/hf_v2/item_parameters_released.rds")) |>
  group_by(item_uid) |>
  summarise(b = mean(difficulty), guessing = first(guessing), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(b)
knitr::kable(released, digits = 2, caption = "Released H&F item difficulties (Rasch, guessing 0.5)")

theta_by_age <- scored_runs |>
  filter(form == "v1", !is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(age = age_band5(age)) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), q10 = quantile(theta, .1), median = median(theta),
            q90 = quantile(theta, .9), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(theta_by_age, digits = 2, caption = "Released θ by age, v1 runs")

# "top decile" below = 90th percentile of v1 children aged 10 and over
top_decile <- unname(quantile(scored_runs$theta[scored_runs$form == "v1" &
                                                  scored_runs$age >= 10], .9, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The hardest released item (a mixed-block switch trial) sits at about +0.6,
while median ability is above 1.7 from age 10 on and the top decile of
children aged 10 and over sits near 3.9, close to the highest score the
model gives. With a 0.5 guessing floor an
item is most informative about half a logit above its difficulty, and its
information can never exceed 0.09 per trial (a 2AFC item carries at most a
quarter of the information of an item with no guessing floor).

```{r item-info}
info_3pl <- \(theta, b, g = 0.5) {
  p <- g + (1 - g) * plogis(theta - b)
  ((p - g) / (1 - g))^2 * (1 - p) / p
}
b_of <- \(uid) released$b[released$item_uid == uid]
at <- theta_by_age |> select(age, theta = median) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(age = "top decile, ages 10+", theta = top_decile))
item_classes <- c(hearts = "hf_hearts_heart_stay", flowers = "hf_flowers_flower_stay",
                  mixed_stay = "hf_heartsflowers_heart_stay",
                  mixed_switch = "hf_heartsflowers_heart_switch")
at |>
  mutate(purrr::map_dfc(item_classes, \(u) info_3pl(theta, b_of(u)))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fisher information per trial at the median θ of each age band (maximum possible: 0.09)")
```

At the median older child, mixed-block switch trials are still fairly
informative (about two-thirds of the maximum). The pure blocks are close to
worthless from age 8 up, and every untimed item gives only about a sixth of
the maximum in the top decile. That top decile is the ceiling.

## Deadline items on the released scale

v1 was untimed, so any deadline D can be imposed after the fact: score a
response correct only if it is on the right side **and** 200 ms ≤ RT ≤ D, then
estimate each item class's difficulty with the children's released θ held
fixed. This puts every hypothetical deadline on the released scale
([`_hf_v2_deadlines.R`](_hf_v2_deadlines.R)).

```{r deadline-items}
dl_file <- here("data/hf_v2/deadline_items.rds")
if (!file.exists(dl_file)) source(here("tasks/_hf_v2_deadlines.R"))
dl <- readRDS(dl_file)

dl$v1_items |>
  mutate(b = if_else(b > 7.9, NA_real_, b)) |>
  select(deadline, item_class, b) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = item_class, values_from = b) |>
  select(deadline, hearts, flowers, mixed_stay, mixed_switch) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Item difficulty (released scale) when a deadline D is imposed on untimed v1 responses. Blank = accuracy below the 0.5 guessing floor, which the model cannot fit.")
```

At D = 2000 ms (the cutoff `recode_hf()` applies today) the counterfactual
difficulties reproduce the released ones, as they should. Tightening to
1500 ms moves the mixed items to about b = 1.3–1.9, right at the older
children's median ability; 1250 ms moves them to about 3–4, the top decile.
Below about 1250 ms accuracy falls under 50%. A model with a 0.5 guessing
floor cannot represent that: a child who misses the window scores 0, not
chance.

```{r wright-map, fig.height = 5.2}
item_lines <- dl$v1_items |>
  filter(is.finite(deadline), b < 7.9) |>
  mutate(item_class = factor(item_class, c("hearts", "flowers", "mixed_stay", "mixed_switch")))
p_items <- ggplot(item_lines, aes(deadline, b, colour = item_class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = theta_by_age$median, colour = "grey75", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = c(3000, 2500, 2000, 1500, 1000),
                  labels = c("3", "2.5", "2", "1.5", "1")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 5)) +
  labs(x = "Imposed deadline (s), faster to the right", y = "Item difficulty (released θ scale)",
       colour = "Item class") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
p_people <- scored_runs |>
  filter(form == "v1", !is.na(age)) |>
  mutate(age = age_band5(age)) |>
  ggplot(aes(age, theta)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, fill = "grey90") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 5)) +
  labs(x = "Age band (v1 children)", y = NULL)
patchwork::wrap_plots(p_items, p_people, widths = c(2, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Where items sit relative to children (shared θ scale)",
    subtitle = "Left: item difficulty with a deadline imposed on untimed v1 responses;\ndotted lines mark each age band's median θ. Right: θ by age.")
```

Read across: at a 3-s deadline (left) every item sits below the median
child aged 6 and over, and the mixed-block items only rise into the 10–12 and
12+ range at about 1.5 s or faster.

The counterfactual can be checked against v2, where children really were
given these windows. Imposing 2000 and 1500 ms on the v2 3-s segment
predicts what the same children did in the 2-s and 1.5-s segments:

```{r deadline-validation}
dl$validation |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) x[!is.na(x)][1])) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Counterfactual vs actual accuracy, v2 runs with all three mixed segments")
```

It matches closely at 2000 ms (.877 vs .875) and slightly underestimates at
1500 ms (.770 vs .801): children speed up a little when the deadline is
real, so the counterfactual is conservative.

```{r deadline-by-age}
typed <- dl$typed
deadline_acc <- \(d) typed |>
  filter(form == "v1", !is.na(age), item_class == "mixed_switch") |>
  group_by(age = age_band5(age)) |>
  summarise(D = d, accuracy = mean(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric >= 200 &
                                     rt_numeric <= d), .groups = "drop")

purrr::map_dfr(c(Inf, 2000, 1750, 1500, 1250, 1000), deadline_acc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = D, values_from = accuracy, names_prefix = "D = ") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Counterfactual accuracy on mixed switch trials by age and imposed deadline (v1 children)")

typed |>
  filter(form == "v2", !is.na(age), item_class == "mixed_switch") |>
  group_by(age = age_band5(age), window) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct %in% TRUE & !timeout), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = window, values_from = accuracy, names_prefix = "window ") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Actual accuracy on mixed switch trials by age and window (v2 children)")
```

In real data the 1.5-s window puts 10–12-year-olds at 83% correct on switch
trials, close to the accuracy at which a 2AFC item with a 0.5 floor is most
informative (about 81%). So that window is well targeted for the median
older child. The 12+ group (88%) and the top decile need something faster:
near 1.25 s in the counterfactual.

## Do shorter windows still measure inhibition and switching?

If a deadline makes items harder on construct, the deadline score should keep
tracking children's switching skill (their untimed mixed-block accuracy), and
the switch-vs-stay contrast should grow. If it only adds speed, the score
should track plain response speed instead, measured here by the median RT on
the easy same-side hearts trials.

```{r construct-check}
partial_r <- \(a, b, z) {
  ok <- complete.cases(a, b, z)
  cor(resid(lm(a[ok] ~ z[ok])), resid(lm(b[ok] ~ z[ok])))
}

v1_base <- typed |>
  filter(form == "v1", !is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(run_id, age) |>
  summarise(untimed_mixed = mean(correct[block == "mixed"] %in% TRUE),
            hearts_rt = median(rt_numeric[block == "hearts"], na.rm = TRUE),
            n_mixed = sum(block == "mixed"), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_mixed == 32)

purrr::map_dfr(c(2000, 1500, 1250, 1000), \(d) {
  sd_ <- typed |>
    filter(form == "v1", block == "mixed") |>
    group_by(run_id) |>
    summarise(score = mean(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric >= 200 &
                             rt_numeric <= d), .groups = "drop") |>
    inner_join(v1_base, by = "run_id")
  tibble(deadline = d,
         r_with_untimed_switching = partial_r(sd_$score, sd_$untimed_mixed, sd_$age),
         r_with_plain_speed = partial_r(sd_$score, sd_$hearts_rt, sd_$age))
}) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Counterfactual (v1): age-partialled correlation of the mixed-block deadline score with untimed switching accuracy and with hearts-block median RT")

typed |>
  filter(form == "v2", block == "mixed") |>
  group_by(window, item_class) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct %in% TRUE & !timeout), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = item_class, values_from = accuracy) |>
  mutate(switch_cost = mixed_stay - mixed_switch) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Actual (v2): stay vs switch accuracy by window")
```

In the counterfactual, the deadline score's link to switching skill
collapses as the window shortens (.47 at 2000 ms, .19 at 1500, .03 at 1250)
while its link to plain speed stays around −.5 to −.6: a short fixed
deadline turns the mixed block into a speed test. Real deadlines change
behaviour, so the v2 data are the stronger test, and they point the same way
by a different route: **the switch cost does not grow as the window
tightens** (.060 at 3 s, .059 at 2 s, .067 at 1.5 s). The deadline adds the
same difficulty to stay and switch trials rather than sharpening the
inhibition and switching contrast.

Two natural alternatives also fail:

```{r alternatives}
hearts_rt_correct <- typed |>
  filter(form == "v1", block == "hearts", correct %in% TRUE) |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(hrt = median(rt_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
indiv <- purrr::map_dfr(c(1.5, 2, 2.5), \(k) {
  sk <- typed |>
    filter(form == "v1", block == "mixed") |>
    inner_join(hearts_rt_correct, by = "run_id") |>
    group_by(run_id) |>
    summarise(score = mean(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric <= k * hrt), .groups = "drop") |>
    inner_join(v1_base |> select(run_id, age, untimed_mixed), by = "run_id") |>
    inner_join(hearts_rt_correct, by = "run_id")
  tibble(window = paste0(k, " × own hearts RT"), mean_accuracy = mean(sk$score),
         r_with_untimed_switching = partial_r(sk$score, sk$untimed_mixed, sk$age),
         r_with_plain_speed = partial_r(sk$score, sk$hrt, sk$age))
})
knitr::kable(indiv, digits = 2, caption = "Counterfactual individualized windows (v1)")

rt_halves <- typed |>
  filter(form == "v1", block == "mixed", correct %in% TRUE) |>
  arrange(run_id, trial_index) |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  mutate(half = row_number() %% 2) |>
  group_by(run_id, half) |>
  summarise(switch_cost = median(rt_numeric[item_class == "mixed_switch"]) -
              median(rt_numeric[item_class == "mixed_stay"]),
            mixed_rt = median(rt_numeric), .groups = "drop")
sb_halves <- \(v) {
  h <- rt_halves |> select(run_id, half, x = all_of(v)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = half, values_from = x)
  r <- cor(h$`0`, h$`1`, use = "complete.obs")
  2 * r / (1 + r)
}
tibble(measure = c("RT switch cost (switch − stay median RT)", "mixed-block median RT"),
       split_half = c(sb_halves("switch_cost"), sb_halves("mixed_rt"))) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Split-half reliability of RT measures, untimed v1 mixed block")
```

A window scaled to each child's own hearts-block speed overcorrects: slower
children end up scoring *higher* (positive correlation with hearts RT). And
the classic ceiling-free alternative, the RT switch cost, is unreliable (a
split-half near zero); mixed-block RT itself is highly reliable but measures
general speed.

## The stop rule is mostly triggered by timeouts

```{r stop-rule-replay}
fires <- function(err) {
  for (i in seq_along(err)) if (sum(err[max(1, i - 9):i]) > 6) return(TRUE)
  FALSE
}
error_out_runs <- runs |> filter(stop_reason %in% "errorOut") |> pull(run_id)
replay <- typed |>
  filter(run_id %in% error_out_runs) |>
  arrange(run_id, trial_index) |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(fires_as_deployed = fires(!(correct %in% TRUE) | timeout),
            fires_without_timeouts = fires(!(correct %in% TRUE) & !timeout),
            timeout_share_last_10 = mean(tail(timeout, 10)),
            age = first(age), .groups = "drop")
replay |>
  summarise(error_out_runs = n(), rule_reproduced = mean(fires_as_deployed),
            would_still_fire_without_timeouts = mean(fires_without_timeouts),
            timeout_share_last_10 = mean(timeout_share_last_10),
            median_age = median(age, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Replaying the error-out rule on the v2 runs it stopped")
```

The rule reproduces exactly from the saved trials, and **72% of the stops
would not have happened if timeouts did not count**. Timeouts are 30% of
these children's last ten trials, and their median age is 6.3: the fast
segments mostly cut off young children.

## What reallocating trials would buy

```{r reallocation}
mix_info <- \(theta, p_switch) p_switch * info_3pl(theta, b_of("hf_heartsflowers_heart_switch")) +
  (1 - p_switch) * info_3pl(theta, b_of("hf_heartsflowers_heart_stay"))
test_info <- \(theta, n_hearts, n_flowers, n_mixed, p_switch)
  n_hearts * info_3pl(theta, b_of("hf_hearts_heart_stay")) +
  n_flowers * info_3pl(theta, b_of("hf_flowers_flower_stay")) +
  n_mixed * mix_info(theta, p_switch)

designs <- tribble(
  ~design, ~n_hearts, ~n_flowers, ~n_mixed, ~p_switch,
  "v2 as deployed (12 + 16 + 48)", 12, 16, 48, 0.62,
  "shorter pure blocks (6 + 8 + 62)", 6, 8, 62, 0.62,
  "shorter pure blocks, 80% switch", 6, 8, 62, 0.80)
targets <- c(`median, 10-12` = theta_by_age$median[theta_by_age$age == "10-12"],
             `top decile, ages 10+` = top_decile)
designs |>
  mutate(purrr::map_dfc(targets, \(t) 1 / sqrt(test_info(t, n_hearts, n_flowers, n_mixed, p_switch)))) |>
  select(design, names(targets)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Expected standard error of θ at a given ability, by trial allocation (released untimed difficulties, same total length; switch share of 62% as observed)")
```

Moving trials from the pure blocks into the mixed block, and raising the
share of switch trials, makes the median older child's score somewhat more
precise at the same test length (SE about 0.53 → 0.48). It helps the top
decile only a little (SE 1.26 → 1.08 at best, still above 1), because every
untimed item is too easy there. Only harder items help much there, and in
this task the only lever the data show is time.

# 10. Scoring alternatives: modelling timeouts, imputing early stops

Two further ideas for getting more out of the v2 data: score each trial with
three outcomes (correct, wrong side, timeout) in a **nominal** IRT model, so
that timeouts can carry different information from errors; and treat a run
that the error-out rule stopped as evidence the child would have kept timing
out, **imputing** the unreached trials.

All models here are fit to the v2 runs only, as a single group, with item
parameters held equal within item class × response window, so the models
differ only in how a trial outcome is coded
([`_hf_v2_nominal.R`](_hf_v2_nominal.R); run with the system R library,
because `mirt` can't load in this project's renv). A trial is correct if the
side is right and RT ≥ 200 ms (no 2000 ms cutoff; v2's windows already bound
RT). Pure-block timeouts (0.2%) are too rare to model and are coded wrong
throughout.

| Model | Trial coding |
|---|---|
| 2PL, timeout = wrong | correct / not (like the released scoring) |
| 2PL, timeout = missing | correct / wrong side; timeouts dropped |
| Nominal | wrong side / timeout / correct, each mixed item with its own category weights |

## How a timeout counts

```{r nominal-weights}
nr <- readRDS(here("data/hf_v2/nominal_results.rds"))
nominal_pars <- as.data.frame(nr$params$nominal) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("item") |>
  mutate(group = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", item)) |>
  filter(grepl("^mixed", group)) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(item_class = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", group),
            window_ms = as.numeric(sub(".*_", "", group)),
            slope = a1, timeout_weight = ak1) |>
  arrange(item_class, desc(window_ms))
knitr::kable(nominal_pars, digits = 2,
             caption = "Nominal model, mixed items: category weights are 0 for a wrong-side response and 2 for a correct one; timeout_weight is where a timeout falls on that scale")
```

The nominal model does find a real distinction. In the 3-s window a timeout
counts *below* a wrong-side response (weight about −1.1 to −1.5): a child who
lets 3 s pass is more likely disengaged than slow. In the 1.5-s window a
timeout counts about the same as an error.

## Imputing early stops: the assumption and the theory

Imputation here fills every trial an error-out run did not reach with a
timeout (mixed block) or an error (pure blocks); the stay/switch status of an
unreached mixed trial is drawn at the observed switch share. Two cautions
apply before looking at any numbers.

First, the stop rule depends only on responses already observed, so the
unreached trials are *ignorably* missing: the EAP score computed from the
observed trials is already the correct use of everything known about the
child. Imputed trials add no information; they are a deterministic function
of trials already in the score. They can only shift the score (by asserting
what the child would have done) and inflate apparent precision.

Second, the assumption that a stopped child would have kept timing out can
be checked on children who came within one error of the rule (six errors in a
ten-trial window) and kept going:

```{r near-miss}
nr$near_miss |>
  summarise(children = n(), median_later_trials = median(next_trials),
            median_accuracy_after = median(acc_after),
            median_timeout_rate_after = median(timeout_after)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Children who reached 6 errors in a 10-trial window but completed the run: their later trials")
```

Most recovered: median 74% correct on later trials, with 6% timeouts. This
group is selected on not having stopped, so it overstates recovery somewhat,
but it is far from the 100% timeouts the imputation assumes.

## Results

```{r scoring-comparison}
model_labels <- c(
  timeout_wrong = "2PL, timeout = wrong",
  nominal = "Nominal",
  timeout_missing = "2PL, timeout = missing",
  `timeout_wrong + imputed` = "2PL, timeout = wrong, error-outs imputed",
  `nominal + imputed` = "Nominal, error-outs imputed")

nr_scores <- bind_rows(nr$scores, nr$imputed_scores) |>
  filter(model %in% names(model_labels))

other_ef <- readRDS(here("data/scores_latest_v3_17.rds")) |>
  filter(task_id %in% c("memory-game", "same-different-selection"), !is.na(score)) |>
  select(user_id, task_id, other_score = score, other_time = time_started)
nr_meta <- runs |>
  semi_join(nr$scores, by = "run_id") |>
  select(run_id, dataset, user_id, age, time_started, stop_reason)
ef_match <- nr_meta |>
  inner_join(other_ef, by = "user_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(gap = abs(as.numeric(difftime(as.POSIXct(other_time, tz = "UTC"),
                                       time_started, units = "days")))) |>
  filter(gap <= 90) |>
  group_by(run_id, task_id) |>
  slice_min(gap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(run_id, task_id, other_score) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = task_id, values_from = other_score)

eval_wide <- nr_scores |>
  select(run_id, model, theta, theta_h0, theta_h1) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(theta, theta_h0, theta_h1),
              names_sep = "|") |>
  inner_join(nr_meta, by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(ef_match, by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n() >= 40) |>
  ungroup()

partial_r <- \(a, b, z) {
  ok <- complete.cases(a, b, z)
  if (sum(ok) < 30) return(NA_real_)
  r <- cor(cbind(a[ok], b[ok], z[ok]))
  (r[1, 2] - r[1, 3] * r[2, 3]) / sqrt((1 - r[1, 3]^2) * (1 - r[2, 3]^2))
}
metrics <- function(d) {
  per_ds <- purrr::map_dfr(split(d, d$dataset), \(x) {
    purrr::map_dfr(names(model_labels), \(m) {
      sh <- cor(x[[paste0("theta_h0|", m)]], x[[paste0("theta_h1|", m)]],
                use = "complete.obs")
      tibble(model = m, n = nrow(x),
             split_half = 2 * sh / (1 + sh),
             r_age = cor(x[[paste0("theta|", m)]], x$age, use = "complete.obs"),
             r_memory = partial_r(x[[paste0("theta|", m)]], x$`memory-game`, x$age),
             r_same_different = partial_r(x[[paste0("theta|", m)]],
                                          x$`same-different-selection`, x$age))
    })
  })
  per_ds |>
    group_by(model) |>
    summarise(across(c(split_half, r_age, r_memory, r_same_different),
                     \(v) sum(v * n, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(n[!is.na(v)])),
              .groups = "drop")
}

point <- metrics(eval_wide)
emp_rel <- nr_scores |>
  inner_join(nr_meta |> select(run_id, dataset), by = "run_id") |>
  semi_join(eval_wide, by = "dataset") |>
  group_by(model, dataset) |>
  summarise(n = n(), rel = var(theta) / (var(theta) + mean(se^2)), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(model_reliability = sum(rel * n) / sum(n), .groups = "drop")

point |>
  left_join(emp_rel, by = "model") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model_labels[model], model_labels)) |>
  arrange(model) |>
  select(model, split_half, model_reliability, everything()) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = sprintf("Reliability and validity by scoring model, v2 runs (%d runs, %d datasets; n-weighted within-dataset values). Memory and Same & Different: age-partialled correlation with the child's nearest run within 90 days.", nrow(eval_wide), n_distinct(eval_wide$dataset)))
```

```{r scoring-bootstrap}
set.seed(20261022)
idx_by_ds <- split(seq_len(nrow(eval_wide)), eval_wide$dataset)
boot <- purrr::map_dfr(1:500, \(b) {
  ii <- unlist(lapply(idx_by_ds, \(i) sample(i, replace = TRUE)))
  metrics(eval_wide[ii, ]) |> mutate(rep = b)
})
boot |>
  pivot_longer(-c(model, rep), names_to = "metric") |>
  group_by(rep, metric) |>
  mutate(diff = value - value[model == "timeout_wrong"]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(model != "timeout_wrong") |>
  group_by(model, metric) |>
  summarise(ci = sprintf("%+.3f [%+.3f, %+.3f]", median(diff),
                         quantile(diff, .025), quantile(diff, .975)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = ci) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model_labels[model], model_labels)) |>
  arrange(model) |>
  select(model, split_half, r_age, r_memory, r_same_different) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Difference from the 2PL timeout = wrong model, with 95% bootstrap intervals (500 paired resamples of runs within dataset)")
```

```{r score-agreement}
eval_wide |>
  summarise(`nominal vs 2PL timeout = wrong` = cor(`theta|nominal`, `theta|timeout_wrong`),
            `2PL timeout = missing vs = wrong` = cor(`theta|timeout_missing`, `theta|timeout_wrong`)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Correlation of full-data scores between models")

eval_wide |>
  filter(stop_reason %in% "errorOut") |>
  summarise(error_out_runs = n(),
            median_shift = median(`theta|nominal + imputed` - `theta|nominal`),
            q10_shift = quantile(`theta|nominal + imputed` - `theta|nominal`, .1)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Effect of imputation on the stopped children's scores (nominal model, logits)")
```

**The nominal model doesn't help.** Its scores correlate .999 with the
dichotomous ones, and every difference in reliability or validity is at most
.004. Because the two sets of scores are nearly identical, the paired
bootstrap can tell some of these tiny differences from zero, but none is
large enough to matter. Timeouts are too rare outside the 1.5-s segment for
their distinct weight to change anyone's score much.

**Timeouts do carry information**: dropping them (timeout = missing) costs
about .04 split-half reliability, .08 in the age correlation, and .04 in the
Memory correlation. Scoring them as errors, as the released model does,
captures that information. The one exception is Same & Different, whose
correlation rises by .02 when timeouts are dropped; that would fit timeouts
adding speed-related variance that an untimed task doesn't share.

**Imputation makes the scores look more reliable and makes them less
valid.** Split-half reliability rises by about .02 and model reliability by
about .03, because the imputed trials sit in both halves and agree by
construction. All three external criteria move the other way, by small
amounts (−.005 to −.012; the intervals for age and Same & Different exclude
zero). The stopped children's scores drop by about half a logit,
which is the imputation asserting an answer to a question the data can't
answer. Don't impute; the observed-trial EAP is already the right score for
a stopped run.

# 11. Refitting both forms on one scale

The released scores can't show whether v2's harder trials stretch the top of
the distribution, because they score v2 with v1's untimed item parameters.
This section recalibrates both forms together
([`_hf_v2_refit.R`](_hf_v2_refit.R), run with `Rscript --vanilla`):

- **One trial coding for both forms:** correct means the right side,
  answered, and 200 ms ≤ RT ≤ the window. The window is 3 s for all of v1 and
  for v2's pure blocks, and v2's actual 3 / 2 / 1.5 s in the mixed segments.
  There is no 2-s recode cutoff.
- **Anchors:** the pure-block items (hearts, flowers) are shared across forms.
  Mixed-block items are form-specific: v1 stay and switch, and v2 stay and
  switch separately for each window.
- **Model:** multigroup by form, Rasch slopes. The guessing floor is either
  fixed at 0.5 for every item (as released) or, for v2's timed mixed items,
  estimated per item group. v1's mean is fixed at 0; both variances and v2's
  mean are free. All runs are included; early stops are ignorable missing
  data.

```{r refit-items}
rf <- readRDS(here("data/hf_v2/refit_results.rds"))
tibble(model = names(rf$logLik), log_likelihood = rf$logLik, parameters = rf$df) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Fit of the two refits")

rf$group_pars |>
  filter(model == "g_estimated") |>
  transmute(form, item_group = group, difficulty = -d, guessing = g) |>
  distinct(item_group, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(difficulty) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Item difficulty and guessing floor, refit with estimated floors for v2's timed items (pure-block anchors shared across forms)")

rf$group_pars |>
  distinct(model, form, mean, var) |>
  mutate(sd = sqrt(var)) |>
  select(-var) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Ability distribution of each form on the refit scale")
```

Estimating the floor for the timed items fits clearly better (log-likelihood
up 48 for 6 parameters). The estimated floors are .25–.41, well below 0.5, as
expected when a missed window scores zero rather than chance. Results below
use that model; the fixed-floor model gives the same picture.

The timed items are harder than their untimed counterparts, as intended: a
1.5-s switch trial sits about 0.6 logits above an untimed v1 switch trial.
But every item is still easier than the average child: the hardest, at about
−0.6, is below the median 10-year-old (0.65 in v2, 0.85 in v1).

```{r refit-theta-by-age, fig.height = 4.8}
refit <- rf$scores |>
  filter(model == "g_estimated") |>
  left_join(runs |> select(run_id, dataset, age, time_started, layout), by = "run_id")

refit |>
  filter(!is.na(age), age >= 4, age < 14) |>
  group_by(form) |>
  mutate(at_max = theta >= max(theta) - 0.05) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(age, theta)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = at_max), alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9) +
  geom_quantile(quantiles = c(.1, .5, .9), formula = y ~ splines::ns(x, 3),
                colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~form) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey55", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      labels = c("below the form's maximum", "at the form's maximum"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "θ (refit, common scale)",
       title = "θ by age on the refit scale",
       subtitle = "All runs with trials. Lines: 10th, 50th, 90th percentiles.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r refit-tables}
refit |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(form, age = age_band5(age)) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), sd = sd(theta), q10 = quantile(theta, .1),
            median = median(theta), q90 = quantile(theta, .9), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "θ by age and form on the refit scale")

refit |>
  filter(grepl("complete \\(", layout), !is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(form) |>
  mutate(form_max = max(theta)) |>
  group_by(form, age = age_band5(age)) |>
  summarise(runs = n(), at_max = mean(theta >= form_max - 0.05),
            within_half_logit = mean(theta >= form_max - 0.5), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = form, values_from = -c(form, age)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Share of complete runs at, or within half a logit of, their form's maximum score")
```

```{r refit-information, fig.height = 4.2}
rf$info_curves |>
  filter(model == "g_estimated", theta >= -4, theta <= 5) |>
  ggplot(aes(theta, info, colour = form)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = quantile(refit$theta[!is.na(refit$age) & refit$age >= 10], c(.5, .9)),
             linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "θ (refit scale)", y = "Test information",
       colour = "Form", title = "Information of a complete run",
       subtitle = "Dotted lines: median and 90th percentile of children aged 10 and over (both forms).")
```

```{r refit-coding}
hf_test |>
  filter(form == "v1", !is.na(block), !is.na(age), age >= 10) |>
  semi_join(complete_runs, by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(run_id) |>
  summarise(within_2s = all(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric >= 200 & rt_numeric <= 2000),
            within_3s = all(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric >= 200 & rt_numeric <= 3000),
            untimed = all(correct %in% TRUE & rt_numeric >= 200), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(across(-run_id, mean)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "v1 complete runs, ages 10+: share with every trial correct under three codings")
```

**The ceiling falls.** In v1, about one in five complete runs from children
10 and over sit at the form's maximum, and 29–34% within half a logit of
it. In v2 those shares are 3–6% and 5–10%. This comparison doesn't depend
on the anchors, since each form is compared with its own maximum. A complete
v2 run also carries 2–3 times the information of a v1 run at θ = 1–4 (part
of that is the 16 extra mixed trials; per mixed trial the gain is about 1.5
times).

v1's ceiling was also worse than the released scores show. Under the 2-s rule
20% of older v1 children make no errors; if every correct answer counts, 38%
do. The released scoring hid half the ceiling by counting slow correct answers
as errors.

**But the range doesn't widen.** v2's spread is narrower than v1's at every
age (SD 1.1–1.6 vs 1.5–2.1). At the bottom that is the feedback lifting the
low end (§7). At the top, the v2 90th percentile sits below v1's because v1's
top is a pile at the cap while v2's is a spread of measured scores, but v2's
hardest items are still easier than most older children. The top is now
resolved rather than stretched: older children are measured with more
precision, within a narrower range.

## Does the anchoring hold?

Using the pure blocks as anchors assumes they are equally difficult in both
forms. Feedback could break that, since it changes how children recover from
errors in exactly those blocks (§7). (The variance comparison above doesn't
depend on the anchors, because in a Rasch model each form's variance is set
by its own data. It does assume equal slopes across forms.) Three sites ran
both forms in the same months, so their age-adjusted means should agree if
the anchoring holds:

```{r anchor-check}
concurrent <- refit |>
  filter(time_started >= as.POSIXct("2026-04-20", tz = "UTC"), !is.na(age)) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n_distinct(form) == 2, min(table(form)) >= 10) |>
  ungroup()
concurrent |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  group_modify(\(x, ...) {
    m <- summary(lm(theta ~ form + age, data = x))$coefficients
    tibble(runs_v1 = sum(x$form == "v1"), runs_v2 = sum(x$form == "v2"),
           mean_age = mean(x$age),
           v2_minus_v1 = m["formv2", "Estimate"], se = m["formv2", "Std. Error"])
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Age-adjusted difference in refit θ (v2 − v1) at sites that ran both forms from April 2026")
```

At Western (mean age 8.4) the two forms agree almost exactly. At UTDT's young
sample (mean age 5.5) v2 children score more than a logit higher. MPIB's v2
sample is too small to say (16 runs; +0.45 ± 0.43). Either the
anchors work differently for young children, which fits feedback helping them
most in the pure blocks, or the two samples differ. So the common scale is
reasonable from about age 7, and cross-form mean comparisons for younger
children shouldn't be trusted.

# Verdict

1. **Variants.** The new form is `taskVersion = 2`, carried by every H&F
   variant created from 2026-04-23 (`English (North America)`, `es-AR`,
   `English (United Kingdom)`, `German (Germany)`, `Spanish (Colombia)`); the
   2025-07-21 variants are v1. Form follows the variant, not the code
   version, and several sites ran both concurrently.
2. **The ding works as feedback** (§7) but compresses the low end of the
   distribution. Keep it if the target construct is efficiency under
   conflict, not rule acquisition.
3. **The floor nearly disappears and the ceiling falls, but the score range
   doesn't widen** (§4, §11). In a refit with the timed items calibrated
   separately, older children at their form's maximum drop from about 19% to
   3–6%, and a complete v2 run gives 2–3 times the information at high
   ability. But the hardest v2 item is still below the median 10-year-old, so
   the top is resolved rather than stretched, and v2's spread is narrower than
   v1's at every age. The faster segments act through timeouts, which also
   drive a large rise in early stops (~25% of v2 runs vs ~8%) via the
   error-out rule.
4. **No reliability gain**: model-based reliability is about equal, split-half
   is lower, and cross-form retest at Leipzig is poor (.12, confounded with
   gap and age).
5. **Shorter fixed windows won't remove the ceiling on construct** (§9).
   They do move items to the older children's abilities (about 1.5 s for the
   median 10–12-year-old, about 1.25 s for the top decile), but the added
   difficulty is generic: the switch cost doesn't grow, and in the
   counterfactual the score drifts from switching skill to plain speed.
   Measuring the top decile with this task means deciding that conflict
   resolution under time pressure is an acceptable construct for older
   children.
6. **Neither scoring alternative helps** (§10). A nominal model that
   separates timeouts from errors gives the same scores and the same
   reliability; imputing timeouts for stopped runs inflates internal
   consistency while slightly lowering external validity.

Recommendations for the DCC:

- **Score v1 and v2 as different forms.** Same item uids are scored with one
  set of parameters, although v2 items differ in difficulty (deadlines,
  feedback). At minimum, add form-specific (or segment-specific) item uids
  and recalibrate; until then, don't interpret θ change across the v1 → v2
  boundary (e.g. Leipzig wave 3) as growth.
- **Align `recode_hf()` with the v2 windows.** A 2000 ms cutoff inside a
  3000 ms window scores coin-rewarded responses as errors. Either cut at the
  window or set the windows to 2 s.
- **Exempt timeouts from the error-out rule** (or turn it off for H&F). That
  alone would have prevented 72% of v2's early stops, mostly of young
  children. The rule's comment and code also disagree (4 vs > 6 of 10).
- **Don't use a 0.5 guessing floor for timed items.** A missed window scores
  0, not chance; calibrate each window separately with a lower or estimated
  floor, which also recovers information from trials already given.
- **Spend trials where the information is:** shorten the pure blocks (they
  are close to worthless from age 8 up, but useful as practice) and give
  the trials to mixed switch trials.
- **If the top decile must be measured,** offer a ~1.25–1.5 s segment only
  to children who do well at 2 s, rather than to everyone; that adds
  information at the top without the young-child error-outs.
- **Keep scoring timeouts as errors** in a dichotomous model, and **don't
  impute early stops**: the score from the observed trials is already
  correct for a stopped run.
- **Plan a v2 → v2 retest** before deciding on the redesign's net value.
